title: Two Sum
description:
Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`.

You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.

### Example
- **Input**: `nums = [2,7,11,15]`, `target = 9`
- **Output**: `[0,1]`

ruby.template:
def two_sum(nums, target)
    # Write your code here
    []
end
ruby.harness:
cases = [
    [[2, 7, 11, 15], 9, [0, 1]],
    [[3, 2, 4], 6, [1, 2]],
    [[3, 3], 6, [0, 1]]
]

passed = 0
cases.each_with_index do |(nums, target, expected), i|
    begin
        res = two_sum(nums, target)
        if res.sort == expected.sort
            passed += 1
        else
            $stderr.puts "Test case #{i} failed: Input #{nums}, Target #{target}. Expected #{expected}, got #{res}"
        end
    rescue => e
        $stderr.puts "Test case #{i} errored: #{e.message}"
    end
end

puts "RESULT:#{passed}/#{cases.length}"

title: Fibonacci Number
description:
The Fibonacci numbers, commonly denoted `F(n)` form a sequence, called the Fibonacci sequence, such that each number is the sum of the two preceding ones, starting from `0` and `1`.

Given `n`, calculate `F(n)`.

### Example
- **Input**: `n = 2`
- **Output**: `1` (F(2) = F(1) + F(0) = 1 + 0 = 1)

ruby.harness:

    [2, 1],

passed = 0
cases.each_with_index do |(n, expected), i|
    begin
        res = fib(n)
        if res == expected
